title: Three-bar space truss: bar forces

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.location: 'V. Axial Stress on a Truss Model' (https://docs.bentley.com/LiveContent/web/STAAD.Pro%20Help-v21/en/GUID-ABE6D61C-8A85-4C02-A566-E2D6D9BD1942.html)
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: Beer and Johnston, Vector Mechanics for Engineers, Statics and Dynamics, 1962, p. 47, problem 2.70 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Space truss: three bars from the pinned joints 1 (0, 0, 0), 2 (8, 0, 0), 3 (0, 6, 0) ft to the joint 4 (4, 2, 6) ft; A = 1 in^2, E = 30e6 psi; 50 lb along +Z at joint 4 (away from the plane of the supports). The page prints the bar stresses; with A = 1 in^2 they equal the bar forces in lb. Statically determinate. Units lb, in. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
